name: Vercel React Best Practices
description: Reviews React and Next.js code for performance costs such as sequential requests, unnecessarily large client bundles, and repeated rendering.
requirements: A React project, the route or diff to review, and ideally a performance trace or bundle report for comparison.
steps: Identify the framework version, rendering model, and a repeatable slow interaction.
Ask the skill to rank findings by impact and propose a targeted change. Measure again using the original scenario.
example: Review the React route that shows our rowing-club fixture list. The race schedule and weather summary load in succession. Identify which requests are independent and show a change that preserves the error states.
check: Inspect the before-and-after network timing and test a failure in each request independently. Check that a weather error still leaves the schedule visible.

name: Website Builder (Landing Page Component System)
description: Assembles a campaign landing page from an existing component library and can save it as a WordPress draft for editorial review.
requirements: An offer, audience, conversion goal, and block library. Creating the draft needs a WordPress connection with draft-editing permissions.
steps: Inventory the available blocks and select the sections needed to explain the offer and support the conversion.
Request copy and a draft page using those blocks. Check the preview link, mobile layout, and form destination.
example: Create a WordPress draft for our Saturday pottery taster. Use the studio’s class hero, instructor card, and booking blocks. The only booking action should point to the taster signup form.
check: Confirm the page status is Draft and the booking link leads to the intended form from the mobile preview.

name: UX Research Interview Kit
description: Produces an interview screener, a timed question guide, a note-taking template, and a way to compare observations across interviews.
requirements: A decision to inform, participant segment, session length, and any constraints on recruitment or recording.
steps: State what the interviews should help decide and who has relevant recent experience.
Request behavioral questions and follow-ups, with space to record direct speech separately from interpretation. Pilot the sequence once.
example: Prepare a 30-minute interview kit for people who booked a community bus in the last month. We need to understand how they selected a pickup point and what they did when their first choice was unavailable.
check: Check that each core question asks about an actual occasion and that the session fits the time limit with room for follow-ups.

name: Persona Workshop Facilitator
description: Builds B2B personas from observed buying decisions and work patterns, with evidence and validation questions for each proposed segment.
requirements: Anonymized interviews, CRM records or win/loss notes, source IDs, and the business decision the personas will inform.
steps: Provide diverse records, identifying repeat observations from the same customer.
Ask for personas grouped by role in the buying decision and the job to accomplish. Mark thin evidence as a hypothesis for the workshop.
example: Use these twelve labeled sales-call summaries to prepare a workshop for a greenhouse scheduling product. Distinguish day-to-day users from purchase approvers only where the records support it.
check: Pick one attribute per persona and trace it to a source. Test whether each persona changes a concrete messaging or product decision.

name: B2B Value Proposition Mapper
description: Connects a buyer’s problem to a product capability, an outcome, and supporting evidence that sales or product teams can substantiate.
requirements: A buyer profile, customer observations, product capabilities, and available evidence such as a demo, quote, or measured result.
steps: Describe the buyer’s current alternative and the cost of the problem in their own terms.
Request a ranked map of claims, evidence, and gaps. Select a headline only after checking that its proof supports the wording.
example: Map our workshop booking software to the concerns in these three fleet-manager interviews. Use the attached demo to support capabilities and mark any time-savings claims that still need measurement.
check: Trace every headline promise to the corresponding capability and proof. Ensure any numerical claim appears in the supplied evidence.

name: Founder Pitch Deck Coach
description: Shapes a pitch into a sequence of defensible claims, with one job per slide, a suggested visual, and a clear ask at the end.
requirements: A deck or outline, audience, speaking time, desired decision, and sources for any numbers or traction claims.
steps: Identify the audience and what they should decide after the presentation.
Request a headline outline, a visual for each claim, and likely objections. Rehearse it against the time limit.
example: Coach a six-minute seed pitch for a rehearsal-room booking startup. Reorder the attached slides around the pilot evidence, put detailed operations in the appendix, and flag unsupported claims.
check: Read only the slide titles to see whether they tell the story. Time a rehearsal and verify the final ask and all quoted metrics.

name: GitHub Actions: Minuten sparen
description: Finds avoidable GitHub Actions runner time in CI and deployment workflows, such as repeated builds, stale runs, and jobs triggered by unrelated changes.
requirements: Workflow YAML and representative recent run durations, plus the checks and release events that must continue to run.
steps: Identify expensive jobs and which kinds of change really need each one. Compare repeated work across runs.
Request targeted changes such as canceling superseded preview runs or reusing a build artifact. Keep protected-branch and release checks covered.
example: Review our static-site workflow and these five Actions timing reports. A README edit currently triggers two preview builds. Suggest a minimal change and explain which checks still run before release.
check: Compare runner minutes on equivalent changes and confirm required checks complete for a documentation change, a source change, and a release.
